oewn-07506178-n.learner: a feeling of very great pleasure or satisfaction.
examples: Elizabeth listened with delight to the happy though modest hopes which Jane entertained of Bingley's regard.
Elizabeth honestly and heartily expressed her delight in the prospect of their relationship.

oewn-05838106-n.learner: a thing or a person that makes someone happy.
examples: It is of all subjects my delight.
That little garden was her chief delight.

oewn-08658688-n.learner: the area around a place, or the area close to it.
examples: Anything beyond the very neighbourhood of Longbourn, I suppose, would appear far.
You must indeed go and see Mr. Bingley when he comes into the neighbourhood.

oewn-08242011-n.learner: the people who live close to one another.
examples: The whole neighbourhood came out to greet the new family.

oewn-04686906-n.learner: the look that a person's face gives.
examples: Mr. Bingley was good-looking and gentlemanlike: he had a pleasant countenance, and easy, unaffected manners.
He spoke of apprehension and anxiety, but his countenance expressed real security.
She raised her countenance to the light of the window.

oewn-06700103-n.learner: official approval that is stated in clear words.
examples: The scheme went forward without the countenance of her guardians.

oewn-05706212-n.learner: the state of not being sure about something.
examples: The advice and entreaty of so near a relation might settle every doubt.
Miss Bingley's letter arrived, and put an end to doubt.

oewn-04764777-n.learner: not being sure whether something is true, or is a fact, or exists at all.
examples: A doubt of his being present had never occurred to her.
She could easily see that he had no doubt of a favourable answer.

oewn-05878206-n.learner: all of a thing, including every part it is made of.
examples: She read the whole of the letter aloud to her sister.

oewn-00003553-n.learner: a group of parts that is thought of as one single thing.
examples: The separate pieces fit together to make a whole.

oewn-04630470-n.learner: the set of feelings and ways of thinking in a person that shape how they usually act and answer things.
examples: By nature inoffensive, friendly, and obliging, his presentation at St. James's had made him courteous.
Mr. Gardiner was a sensible, gentlemanlike man, greatly superior to his sister, as well by nature as education.
Two offences of a very different nature, and by no means of equal magnitude, you last night laid to my charge.
It was not in her power to give any information of so satisfactory a nature as the compliment deserved.

oewn-04733982-n.learner: the basic qualities of something, by which people know what it is.
examples: Jane and Elizabeth attempted to explain to her the nature of an entail.

oewn-09526814-n.learner: the power that makes and controls the things of the universe.
examples: Nature has made some animals stronger than others.

oewn-08578489-n.learner: the space within which the eye can see.
examples: Every turning expected to bring it in view.
Mr. Collins was walking the whole morning within view of the lodges opening into Hunsford Lane.

oewn-05992348-n.learner: the purpose someone has in mind in doing something.
examples: It remains to be told why my views were directed to Longbourn instead of my own neighbourhood.
He had rather hoped that all his wife's views on the stranger would be disappointed.

oewn-05941982-n.learner: what you see when you look out over an area.
examples: Its windows, opening to the ground, admitted a most refreshing view of the high woody hills behind the house.

oewn-00032194-r.learner: before a time that is named or understood.
examples: He is gone to my father already.
She had been graciously pleased to approve of both the discourses which he had already had the honour of preaching before her.

oewn-04630969-n.learner: the mood a person is usually in.
examples: We are each of an unsocial, taciturn disposition, unwilling to speak.
Remember, Eliza, that he does not know Jane's disposition as you do.

oewn-06206319-n.learner: a way of thinking that leans toward one choice rather than the others.
examples: He listened with a disposition to believe the best of her.

oewn-04950046-n.learner: a habit or usual tendency that a person or a thing has, either from birth or picked up later.
examples: The old door has a disposition to stick in wet weather.

oewn-07509503-n.learner: hurt in the mind; a deep feeling that people try to keep away from.
examples: She can have no idea of the pain she gives me by her continual reflections on him.
I knew that what I wrote must give you pain, but it was necessary.

oewn-14346126-n.learner: a hurt in the body that is a sign of an injury or an illness.
examples: The pain in his side was the first sign that something was wrong.

oewn-05732639-n.learner: a sharp feeling of hurt in the body.
examples: He felt a sudden pain as his hand touched the hot pan.
